source: CK-12 Middle School Math Grade 7, Section 6.2, CC-BY-NC
notes: Class B document (13 units). Eighth mathematics document, final document to bring the corpus to 40. Covers the balance method for solving one-variable linear equations with a two-part worked example. One ECU.

units.label: Hook: balance scale analogy (image)
units.content_summary: Illustration of a balance scale with unknown weight 'x' plus 3kg on one side and 10kg on the other, perfectly level. Caption: 'An equation is a balance — whatever you do to one side, do to the other.'

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: apply inverse operations to isolate a variable; solve one-step and two-step linear equations; check a solution by substitution.

units.label: The balance principle (text)
units.content_summary: To solve an equation, isolate the variable by performing the same inverse operation on both sides, keeping the equation balanced. Addition undoes subtraction; multiplication undoes division, and vice versa.

units.label: One-step equation example (text)
units.content_summary: Solve x + 3 = 10: subtract 3 from both sides → x = 7. Solve 4x = 20: divide both sides by 4 → x = 5. Both shown with the inverse operation applied to both sides simultaneously.

units.label: Two-step equation procedure (text)
units.content_summary: For equations like 2x + 3 = 11: first undo addition/subtraction (subtract 3: 2x=8), then undo multiplication/division (divide by 2: x=4). Order matters — reverse the order of operations.

units.label: Two-step diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Step-by-step visual showing 2x+3=11 with each transformation shown on a balance scale: removing 3 from both sides, then splitting into two equal groups.

units.label: Worked example: 3x - 5 = 16 (text)
units.content_summary: Full worked solution: 3x-5=16 → add 5 to both sides → 3x=21 → divide both sides by 3 → x=7. Check: 3(7)-5=21-5=16 ✓. Every step shown with justification.

units.label: Worked example verification diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram showing the check step: substituting x=7 back into the original equation 3x-5=16, computing both sides, confirming they match.

units.label: Checking your solution (text)
units.content_summary: Always verify a solution by substituting it back into the ORIGINAL equation (not an intermediate step). If both sides are equal, the solution is correct.

units.label: Video: solving equations practice (video)
units.content_summary: Video working through three additional two-step equations at increasing difficulty, narrating the inverse-operation reasoning at each step.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Five equations to solve: x-4=9; 5x=35; 2x+7=19; 4x-3=17; x/3+2=6. Each requiring identification of the correct inverse operations.
